$comment: Risk-control → test binding manifest. Created as CAPA-001 action PA-1.
CAPA-001 root cause: 'The verification process accepts unexecuted,
unreproducible, self-attested prose as objective evidence for risk-control
implementation, and nothing in the build pipeline can contradict it.'
This file is the contradiction mechanism. Every risk control whose status is
'implemented' MUST name test node IDs that exist and pass. The manifest is
a named test has disappeared. Deleting a risk control's test therefore turns
CI red instead of producing a silent green build.
implemented  - control exists in code AND is bound to passing tests.
'tests' must be non-empty and every entry must resolve.
not_implemented - control does not exist. Recorded honestly. 'tests' empty.
deliberately_absent - the code intentionally does NOT provide this control;
unverified   - not yet re-verified to the CAPA-001 standard. Must not be
recorded as VERIFIED in the RMF until it is.
A control may only be recorded VERIFIED in the Risk Management File when its
capa_reference: CAPA-001, CAPA-002, CAPA-004, CAPA-005, CAPA-006, CAPA-007

RC-023.description: Anatomical orientation is determinable from the affine, and is never guessed when indeterminate
RC-023.negative_control: CAPA-004 CA-4.1 — fixed RAS return → 9 failed; canonicalisation neutralised → 2 failed. CA-4.2 — orientation warning silenced in the viewport → 2 failed
RC-023.note: NEW control created by CAPA-004 CA-4.1; MUST be added to the Risk Management File §5.1 (tracked). It provides the primitives only. RC-013 — orientation VALIDATION ON UPLOAD — remains not_implemented because canonicalisation is deliberately opt-in: image and mask load through separate calls, so transforming one and not the other would misalign them and create a worse hazard than the one being fixed. Migrating to canonical-by-default must convert both together in one change, with a matched-pair correspondence test. The viewport now REPORTS the orientation and warns when it is UNKNOWN or non-canonical, but deliberately renders NO L/R edge labels: volumes are not canonicalised on load and imaging_service transposes with fixed axis tuples presuming RAS, so the axis-to-screen mapping is unverified. A test asserts that absence. Labels may only be added under CA-4.3, after verification against a phantom of known laterality.

RC-026.description: Object-level authorization for patient records under the care-team entitlement model
RC-026.implementation: app/security/patient_access.py (pure decision) + app/services/care_team_service.py (assignment store) + app/security/patient_access_dependency.py (HTTP guard) + app/api/routes/patients.py (6 patient-scoped routes + care-team management)
RC-026.negative_control: decision layer — 4 vectors (7/2/1/7 failed); enforcement layer — 3 vectors: guard removed from a route -> 1 failed; enforcement returns patient unconditionally -> 7 failed; 403 instead of 404 (enumeration leak) -> 1 failed
RC-026.note: ENFORCED on the PATIENT resource: all 6 patient-scoped routes (get/update/delete + 3 medical-history) plus care-team management now call require_patient_access, which denies with 404 (never 403) to prevent patient enumeration. Care-team assignment/revocation themselves require object access, so a clinician cannot add themselves to a team they are not on; ADMIN bootstraps. STILL OPEN under CAPA-002: imaging.py, studies.py and documents.py are NOT yet wired — they identify the patient indirectly (via file_id / study_id), which needs CA-2.3 (opaque IDs resolved server-side) first. CAPA-002 remains OPEN until those routes enforce access and CA-2.3 lands. ERRATUM 2026-10-17 (CAPA-009): the HTTP guard did not execute. require_patient_access was a plain def returning a coroutine that FastAPI never awaited; the enforcement tests matched source text and called the decision function directly, so they could not observe it. Fixed (async def) and bound by request to tests/unit/test_capa009_object_authorization_everywhere.py (RC-036).

RC-027.note: Closes the imaging half of CAPA-002. Malformed references and cross-patient references both return an identical 404 (no enumeration oracle over key space or patient space). object_path is rebuilt from parsed components, so no unparsed caller byte reaches the storage key. SCOPE: patient-scoped imaging grammar only. Segmentation objects (segmentations/{id}/...) and the studies/documents routes are NOT yet covered — CAPA-002 remains OPEN for those.

RC-028.description: Object-level authorization on study, series, instance and document routes; list routes are patient-scoped
RC-028.implementation: app/security/resource_access.py (resolve object -> patient_id, then reuse RC-026) + app/api/routes/studies.py (12 routes) + app/api/routes/documents.py (6 routes)
RC-028.negative_control: 3 vectors, each measured in a single isolated run (chained runs retired): guard grants on unresolved patient (patient_id=None) -> 1 failed; a resolver raises instead of returning None -> 2 failed; unscoped listing allowed for non-admin -> 1 failed
RC-028.note: Resolves each object to its owning patient (study.patient_id direct; series/instance via study_id; document.patient_id direct) and authorizes via the RC-026 decision. Unresolved objects and unauthorized patients both return an identical 404 (no id enumeration). List routes require a patient_id scope for non-admins — an unscoped archive-wide listing is the bulk form of the CAPA-002 defect. SCOPE NOTE: series/instance resolution relies on the study service's existing full-collection scan (a pre-existing N+1); correct but not yet efficient. RC-029.description: Object-level authorization on segmentation routes; create authorizes the target image; list is file-scoped
RC-029.implementation: app/security/resource_access.py::resolve_segmentation_patient_id + authorize_file_scope (resolve via metadata.file_id -> extract_patient_id_from_path) + app/api/routes/segmentation.py (12 object routes + create + list); CAPA-007 (2026-10-17): app/security/resource_access.py::authorize_mask_specs (body-referenced segmentations and instances) + app/api/routes/segmentation_analysis.py (lesion-analysis, dis-assessment, lesion-annotations, export/dicom-seg depend on require_segmentation_access; compare, agreement-map, longitudinal/compare, longitudinal/sel call authorize_mask_specs; client gcs_path no longer used); the region routes (CAPA-006)
RC-029.negative_control: 2 vectors, each in a single isolated run: resolver invents a patient for a non-patient file_id -> 2 failed; unscoped listing allowed for a non-admin -> 1 failed; CAPA-007 (2026-10-17, scripts/safety/rc029_negative_controls.py): 11 mutations on the analysis routes, 11 detected; restored 12 passed (record docs/iec62304/records/risk_verification/RC-029_analysis_negative_controls_2026-10-17.json)
RC-029.note: Last data surface of CAPA-002. A segmentation stores no patient_id — it stores the file_id of the image it segments, which is patient-scoped; the owning patient is extracted from that file_id (reusing RC-027). Non-patient or malformed file_ids fail closed to a 404. create authorizes request.file_id via the imaging guard (a caller may only segment an image they can access). list requires a file_id scope for non-admins and authorizes every referenced patient. With RC-026/027/028/029, all patient, imaging, study, document and segmentation data routes now enforce object-level access. ERRATUM 2026-09-28 (CAPA-006 Finding 10): the wiring test read segmentation.py only; the ten routes split out into segmentation_regions.py / segmentation_analysis.py by the C3 refactor (5ebe5f6, 2026-07-10) had authentication only. classify-regions and generate-zone-map are now authorized and tested in tests/unit/test_rc032_region_atlas_guard.py (CAPA-006); the eight analysis routes are open under CAPA-007. CAPA-007 (2026-10-17): the eight analysis routes are now authorized; the authorization test enumerates the routes the APP MOUNTS (not a file), so a route moved by a refactor can no longer escape. Approved by N. G. Bonilla Vargas 2026-10-17 (PR #45).

RC-030.description: Discrete lesions are labelled with 18-connectivity (ISBI-2015/MSSEG-2016), and the min-lesion-volume noise floor is a single documented MSSEG-2016 constant
RC-030.implementation: backend/app/services/lesion_metrics.py (shared 18-conn structuring element + MIN_LESION_VOLUME_MM3) used by lesion_analysis_service.py (3 sites), ms_region_classifier.py (3 sites), longitudinal_tracking_service.py (1 site)
RC-030.negative_control: revert label_lesions to scipy's default (6-connectivity) -> 3 failed
RC-030.note: Evidence: deep-research 2026-07-27, 22 claims confirmed. scipy.ndimage.label defaulted to 6-connectivity, which over-counts vs the two reference challenges that both use 18-connectivity. The 3.0 mm3 floor is re-anchored to MSSEG-2016's evaluation gate and explicitly NOT the 3 mm-DIAMETER (~14 mm3) diagnostic criterion (the old '~3 voxels' justification was conflatable and is removed); the duplicated literal is consolidated. Longitudinal tracking now applies the same noise floor. CHANGES REPORTED LESION COUNT and DIS region-presence — a risk-controlled clinical change. HONEST LIMITS: 18-conn is the challenge-EVALUATION standard, not a clinical consensus; CC labelling cannot separate confluent lesions, so count is inherently less reliable than volume/load (rho ~0.92-0.97 vs ~0.83-0.94). Class C modules changed (lesion_analysis, ms_region_classifier) — needs review.

RC-032.negative_control: Executed 2026-10-17 against the final code by scripts/safety/rc032_negative_controls.py, one mutation at a time (application of each asserted), failing test names recorded in docs/iec62304/records/risk_verification/RC-032_negative_controls_2026-09-28.json. Not detected BY DESIGN (redundant sub-controls, stated in the record): the two route MNI gates (each covered by the service gate; detected together in AB and F) and the diagonal-dominance condition (covered by the per-axis FOV condition). No unexpected undetected mutation. RC-032.note: CAPA-006. Motivation measured (scripts/safety/haz005_atlas_misregistration_probe.py, docs/research/records/haz005_atlas_misregistration_output.txt run 2): moving the anatomy by up to 3 deg / 3 % / 5 mm inside an MNI grid changed the MAGNIMS region of 216/786 expert lesions (27.5 %) and brain DIS in 4/30 scans.
